instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.1 Wage and Hour Act - local governments preempted
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: State Wage and Hour Act supersedes and preempts any local ordinance imposing requirements on employers on compensation, wage levels, hours, payment of earned wages, benefits, leave or well-being of minors (S.L. 2023-134 s.5.9(a)); exceptions only for a local government's own employees, economic-development incentives, CDBG, G.S. 160D-1311 programs. Result: no local minimum wage and no local paid-leave mandate on private employers in NC.

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.3 Minimum wage
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage = higher of 6.15 USD/h or the FLSA 29 USC 206(a)(1) rate as it changes (federal 7.25 USD/h, see FED unit) -> 7.25 USD/h in 2026; no state indexation. Full-time students, learners, apprentices, messengers: 90% of the (a) rate rounded to the lowest nickel (7.25 x 0.9 = 6.525 -> 6.50 USD/h, derived). Tip credit only up to the FLSA 3(m) amount, with advance notice, retention of all tips and monthly/per-period tip certification; tip pool may not reduce an employee's tips by more than 15%.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read); 90% student rate derived arithmetically

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.4 Overtime
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime at not less than 1.5 x regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek; no daily overtime.

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.5 Youth employment
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Under-18 workers need a youth employment certificate issued by the Commissioner of Labor unless exempted; school-term night-work limit 11 p.m.-5 a.m. for youths enrolled in grade 12 or lower (16-17 may work later with parent and principal written approval).

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.6 Wage payment (pay frequency)
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: All wages and tips paid on the regular payday; pay periods may be daily, weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly or monthly; bonuses/commissions/other calculated wages may be paid as infrequently as annually if prescribed in advance. No direct-deposit or paycard rule in this section.

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.7 Payment to separated employees
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Separated employees (any reason: discharge and resignation alike) paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday, through regular pay channels or by trackable mail if the employee requests in writing; bonuses/commissions paid on the first regular payday after the amount becomes calculable; forfeiture only if notified per G.S. 95-25.13.

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.8 Withholding of wages (deduction authorization)
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Deductions allowed when required by law, or with signed written authorization stating reason and amount/percentage (known amount) or reason plus advance written notice of actual amount and right to withdraw (unknown amount). Deductions for the employer's benefit may reduce pay only to minimum wage and never overtime wages; cash/inventory shortage or property damage needs 7 days' written notice (not at separation). Overpayments by bona fide error, wage advances and loan principal are prepayment of wages and deductible. Authorization/notice may be electronic (UETA).

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.12 Vacation pay plans
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: No duty to provide vacation; if provided, time off or payment in lieu per company policy/practice; forfeiture of accrued vacation (incl. at separation) only if the employee was notified of the forfeiture policy per G.S. 95-25.13 (13 NCAC 12 .0805(c): unwritten forfeiture policy unenforceable).

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.14 Exemptions from minimum wage, overtime, youth employment
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Exempt from state MW/OT/youth rules: FLSA-covered enterprise employees (FLSA governs instead), agriculture, domestic workers incl. babysitters/companions, bona fide volunteers, etc. Exempt from MW and OT: summer camps, seafood, employer's spouse/child/parent/dependent, FLSA executive/administrative/professional/outside sales, computer professionals, minor-league baseball. Exempt from OT only: drivers/loaders/mechanics, taxi drivers, seamen/rail/air, auto/truck/farm-implement dealer salespersons and mechanics, live-in child-care workers, seasonal amusement. State and local government: only minimum wage, definitions, exemptions and complainant protection apply.

instrument_name: G.S. 105-153.5 Modifications to adjusted gross income (standard deduction)
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: NC standard deduction: MFJ/surviving spouse 25,500; head of household 19,125; single 12,750; MFS 12,750 USD. These are the amounts built into NC-30 2026 (12,750 single; 19,125 HoH), reconciled arithmetically against US-NC-001.
verification_method: derived arithmetically (NC-30 per-period deduction = statute amount / pay periods)

instrument_name: G.S. 105-153.7 Individual income tax imposed (rate and rate-reduction trigger)
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Flat rate 3.99% for taxable years after 2025. Trigger (a1): if total General Fund revenue in FY 2025-26 exceeds 33,042,000,000 USD (OSC final accounting, August following FY end), the 2027 rate = greater of prior rate minus 0.50 pp or 2.49% (i.e. 3.49%); further triggers FY2026-27 34.1bn -> 2028 ... FY2031-32 -> 2034. Withholding tables authorised by (b).

instrument_name: G.S. 105-163.1 Withholding definitions
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee = resident or nonresident performing services in NC for wages, or resident performing services outside NC; includes clergy electing employee treatment under 105-163.1A, corporate officers and elected public officials. Wages = IRC 3401 meaning, except nonresident disaster-response work for critical infrastructure companies during a disaster response period.

instrument_name: G.S. 105-228.90 Revenue Act definitions - Code conformity date
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: 'Code' = Internal Revenue Code as enacted as of July 5, 2025 (updated by S.L. 2026-31, formerly January 1, 2023). Payroll exclusions (401(k) deferrals, s.125, HSA, transit, group-term life) therefore follow federal treatment for withholding; NC-30 s.22: state wages reported to the same extent as federal.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read); second independent authority (NCDOR notice US-NCS5-029)

instrument_name: G.S. 96-9.2 Required contributions to the Unemployment Insurance Fund
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI contributions employer-only: employer may not deduct contributions from remuneration. Beginning employer rate 1%; experience rate = base (2.9% / 2.4% / 1.9% by trust-fund ratio) minus ERRP (reserve ratio x 0.68), rounded to 0.01%, min 0.06%, max 5.76%.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read); second independent authority (DES page US-NCP9V-001)

instrument_name: G.S. 96-9.3 Determination of taxable wages (UI wage base indexation)
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base = greater of the FUTA base or 50% of the average yearly insured wage (average weekly wage at the computation date x 52), rounded to the nearest 100 USD; determined each calendar year by DES. Wages paid in another state with contributions there, and predecessor wages on successorship, count toward the base. 2026 value 34,200 (US-NC-002 / US-NCP9V-001).

instrument_name: G.S. 75-62 Social security number protection
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Business may not make an SSN available to the general public, print it on access cards, require unsecured internet transmission, or print it on materials mailed to the individual unless state/federal law requires it; a mailed SSN may not be visible on a postcard/envelope; redacted SSNs exempt. No NC rule mandating SSN truncation on the pay statement itself located.

instrument_name: G.S. 1-362 Debtor property ordered sold - earnings exemption
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Earnings for personal services within the 60 days preceding the order cannot be applied to a judgment when shown necessary for the support of the debtor's family: no general creditor wage garnishment for ordinary civil judgments in NC (statutory exceptions: child support, state taxes, etc.).

instrument_name: G.S. 110-136 Garnishment for enforcement of child-support obligation
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Child-support garnishment order may not exceed 40% of the responsible parent's monthly disposable earnings (disposable = after legally required withholdings); amount garnished increased by a 1 USD processing fee per pay period, retained by the employer.

instrument_name: G.S. 110-136.4 Implementation of income withholding in IV-D cases
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: IV-D income withholding: obligee serves the payor with notice to withhold within 45 days of the obligor's receipt of advance notice, by Rule 5 service or by federal OCSE e-IWO electronic transmission. Payor-duty subsections (remittance timing, payor fee) not extracted in this pass.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read, subsection (a) only)

instrument_name: G.S. 110-129.2 State Directory of New Hires
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Every NC employer reports each new employee for whom a federal W-4 is required within 20 days of hire (or, if transmitting electronically twice monthly, transmissions 12-16 days apart); content: employee name, address, SSN, first date services performed, employer name, address and FEIN.

instrument_name: G.S. 105-242 Collection of tax - attachment and garnishment
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: NCDOR attachment/garnishment: no more than 10% of a taxpayer's wages or salary is subject to attachment and garnishment for state tax debts; public employees' wages also attachable.

instrument_name: 13 NCAC 12 .0802 Record retention
authority: NC Office of Administrative Hearings - NC Administrative Code (13 NCAC 12, NC Department of Labor rules)
figure_or_rule_carried: All records, posted notices and writings required by the Wage and Hour Act retained 3 years unless another period is stated.

instrument_name: 13 NCAC 12 .0805 Notification during employment
authority: NC Office of Administrative Hearings - NC Administrative Code (13 NCAC 12, NC Department of Labor rules)
figure_or_rule_carried: G.S. 95-25.13(2) notice satisfied by an up-to-date handbook or by payroll records incl. check stubs where hourly/salary terms are identifiable; promised wages payable even under unwritten policy; unwritten forfeiture policies for vacation, commissions, bonuses unenforceable.

instrument_name: 13 NCAC 12 .0807 Methods of providing employees with itemized statement of deductions
authority: NC Office of Administrative Hearings - NC Administrative Code (13 NCAC 12, NC Department of Labor rules)
figure_or_rule_carried: Itemized statement of deductions (G.S. 95-25.13(4)) may be given in writing, by e-mail if printable, or by any other means giving the information in a form the employee can retain in writing: electronic pay statements allowed, no separate consent rule.

instrument_name: NC DES - File, Adjust or Review Quarterly Tax & Wage Report
authority: NC Division of Employment Security (NC Department of Commerce)
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly Tax and Wage Report (NCUI 101) for each quarter from the first quarter of employment; wages by employee name and SSN; due Apr 30 / Jul 31 / Oct 31 / Jan 31; 10 or more employee wage items -> electronic filing mandatory (NCSUITS online or file upload), else 25 USD penalty; paper only for 9 or fewer; zero report required while in business. Late filing 5% per month max 25%; late payment 10%; interest under G.S. 105-241.21(i).

instrument_name: NC DES - Understanding Wage Audit Notices vs. Separation Notices
authority: NC Division of Employment Security
figure_or_rule_carried: DES separation notice is reactive: sent to the employer when a former employee files a UI claim; employer gives separation reason, last day worked and final pay details by the deadline on the notice. Not evidence of a proactive employer separation-notice duty (open question).

instrument_name: NCDOR Form NC-3 File Layout Specifications (NC-3 Format 10-2020)
authority: NC Department of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: eNC3 accepts only .txt fixed files; record length 512; monthly withholding amounts Jan-Dec in dollars-and-cents fields; withholding account number numeric. EDITION IS 10-2020 (references TY2020): not the TY2026 edition; TY2026 = NC3 spec version 9-2026 listed in US-NCS5-028 (not downloaded). Use only as structural lead.

instrument_name: NCDOR eNC3 File Format Specifications page
authority: NC Department of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: eNC3 Web File Upload: fixed-field .txt files for NC-3 and W-2; .xml for 1099/W-2G/1042-S, per IRS/SSA/NCDOR specs. TY2026 specs (use beginning January 2027): NC-3, NC-3X, W-2, W-2C, W-2G, 1042S, 1099s all version 9-2026; TY2025 specs version 9-2025. NC-3 + state W-2s due January 31 (NC-30 s.23, US-NC-001).

instrument_name: NCDOR Important Notice - impact of recently enacted laws (S.L. 2026-31, S.L. 2026-41) on NC individual and corporate income tax
authority: NC Department of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: S.L. 2026-31 (signed July 2026) updated the IRC reference to July 5, 2025 (from January 1, 2023); new R&E decoupling (105-153.6A), Helene timber casualty deduction, gambling-loss itemized deduction (S.L. 2026-41). Notice dated 2026-07-23, updated 2026-07-29 and 2026-10-09. Operates at assessment (return) level, not withholding; no change to NC-30 withholding announced.

instrument_name: NCGA Fiscal Research Division - May 2026 Consensus Revenue Forecast Revision Summary
authority: NC General Assembly Fiscal Research Division (consensus forecast with OSBM)
figure_or_rule_carried: Forecast, not a determination: triggers expected to be exceeded in FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 -> PIT rate 3.99% (2026) -> 3.49% (2027) -> 2.99% (2028+). Binding determination = OSC final accounting of FY2025-26 GF revenue (August 2026) under G.S. 105-153.7(a1), not located.

instrument_name: OSBM memo - 2025-26 General Fund appropriations, authorized revenues and condition of the fund (SL 2026-1)
authority: NC Office of State Budget and Management
figure_or_rule_carried: Authorized (budgeted) FY2025-26 General Fund revenue schedules as ratified by SL 2026-1: an estimate, not the OSC final accounting the trigger statute requires. Context for the 2027 rate question only.
